name: evaluate-fix-ladder
body:
Evaluate the fix ladder and let the plan choose from evidence, not assumption. The design space that must be assessed:
(a) serialize the WHOLE durable mutation sequence under one wait-not-fail file lock — extend the `apg.artifacts.acquire_spec_lock` flock so the node/edge path participates for the entire mutation: the node-file read-modify-write (`edge_add` reads the source file, src/node_cmd.rs:207; `node_rm` rewrites every referencing file), every DB open, and the commit (`git::commit_files`, src/git.rs:587-645, whose `repo.index()` / `index.add_path` / `index.write()` create and hold git's `.git/index.lock`). A lock covering only the DB is insufficient.
(b) bounded retry/backoff around a contended open — a last resort, never the primary fix.
(c) remove DB access from the mutation path — validate structural references from the node files and code-FQN references from a cached symbol index or `apg/.trans/graph.jsonl`. This removes DB contention ONLY. It is NOT structurally race-free: the node-file read-modify-write still races (two parallel `edge add`s on the same source lose an edge, last write wins) and the commit still contends on `.git/index.lock`. It is a complement, never a standalone fix.
(d) a session-scoped single-writer mutation coordinator — a coordinator that owns the whole durable mutation (node-file RMW + commit + projection record) and the DB imposes one order on everything, so it too makes the sequence serial-equivalent while a session is live. It is the project's mandatory amortization + batching deliverable (session-mutation-coordinator).

Honest derivation: option (c) alone cannot meet the acceptance — serial-equivalence requires file-level serialization (a) or a single writer (d). Chosen race fix: (a), file-level serialization over the whole durable sequence, because `concurrent-bursts-reliable` must hold for the transparent direct path too (an agent that never starts a session still issues `apg node` / `apg edge`). (d) is MANDATORY (not a contingent fallback) for its amortization + batching win and serializes while a session is live, but it cannot be the only guarantee because sessions are explicit; it is justified by amortization + batching, not merely lock avoidance. (c) is a complement that removes DB contention in either case; (b) is a last resort. Each option is scored on the project laws (durable-state authority, one-commit-per-mutation, unchanged tool surface) and the acceptance criteria. Acceptance: a recorded evaluation covering all four options that states (b)/(c) alone are insufficient, names (a) as the chosen race fix with (d) the mandatory single-writer/amortization deliverable, and cites the node-file RMW and the git index lock as the races that outlive a DB-only fix.
